skill.name: Persuasive tricks: exaggeration, "everyone's doing it", rhetorical questions
skill.why: Persuaders use tricks to push you. Spot the trick and it loses its power.
skill.how: Ask: is it blown up, 'join the crowd', or a question with the answer built in?

beats.say: Persuaders have three favourite tricks. Let's catch them.
Exaggeration makes things sound way bigger than they are.
beats.show: My pies are **so hot they could melt a ute**.

beats.say: 'Everyone's doing it' says join the crowd or miss out.
beats.show: **Your mates have already signed up.** Don't get left behind!

beats.say: A rhetorical question has its answer built in.
Spot the trick. Then ask: is it actually true?

encounters.frame: A ferry company has mailed a glossy brochure to every house on Bluster Rock. Tully is comparing it with the bus timetable.
encounters.text: INTRODUCING THE BLUSTER EXPRESS. From the first of March, our brand-new passenger ferry will run between Bluster Rock and the mainland six times a day, seven days a week. The ferry seats 120 passengers on two decks, with a cafe on the lower deck and an open-air viewing platform at the top, where dolphins are often spotted in the channel. The crossing takes forty minutes in calm weather, and bicycles can travel free of charge. Adult tickets are $18 each way, and children under twelve travel for half price. At the moment, the only other way to reach the mainland is the coast road, a three-hour drive around the bay. Why would anyone endure three hours behind the wheel when they could be sipping a hot chocolate on the water? Tickets can be bought online or at the kiosk on the jetty. Tully checked the bus timetable and found that the coast road really does take three hours. She also worked out that the ferry would save her family about 120 hours of driving a year, which she has written on the fridge.

encounters.success: A rhetorical question. The brochure isn't asking you. It builds in the answer: nobody would, so take the ferry.

encounters.frame: The new Red Rock Wildlife Park has printed a brochure. Wren read it with a pencil in her hand, marking every trick.
encounters.text: WELCOME TO THE RED ROCK WILDLIFE PARK. Nestled at the foot of Bluster Rock, our park is home to more than forty species of native animals, from tiny dunnarts to towering emus. Our keepers care for injured and orphaned animals and, where possible, return them to the wild. The park covers twelve hectares and is open from 9 am to 5 pm every day except Christmas Day. Our walk-through aviary is so enormous that birds have been known to get lost on their way to lunch. Thousands of families have already made the park their favourite day out, so don't be the one still sitting at home. Who could resist the chance to meet a bilby up close? Keeper talks are held every hour on the hour, and visitors can help feed the kangaroos at 2 pm. Entry costs $22 for adults and $11 for children, and all money goes towards the animals' care. The park cafe sells sandwiches, ice creams and hot drinks, and picnic tables are set out under the coolabah trees beside the waterhole.
